articles.body: Singapore Maintains Role Leading Maritime City in 2026 Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 13, 2026 © Adobe Stock/lena Ermakova Singapore has retained its position as the world’s leading maritime city in the 2026 Leading Maritime Cities (LMC) report by DNV and Menon Economics for the seventh consecutive edition. Singapore also maintained its leading position in three of the five pillars* assessed in the report — Shipping, Ports and Logistics, and Attractiveness and Competitiveness. The LMC report benchmarks leading maritime cities based on objective indicators, including shipping activity, port performance and maritime business services, as well as assessments by maritime industry experts worldwide. Home to over 200 international shipping groups and a wide range of maritime service providers, Singapore’s continued recognition as a leading maritime city reflects the strength of its maritime ecosystem, which brings together global connectivity, port and logistics capabilities, maritime services, talent and innovation. These complementary strengths provide maritime companies with access to markets, business opportunities and specialized expertise, making Singapore an attractive location for companies to establish their presence and grow their businesses. This ecosystem is supported by Singapore’s position as one of the world’s busiest ports, connected to more than 600 ports worldwide. In 2025, the Port of Singapore handled a record 44.66 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in container throughput and 3.22 billion gross tonnage in vessel arrival. Singapore also remained the world’s largest bunkering port, with marine fuel sales reaching a record 56.77 million tonnes. Continued investments in port automation, maritime digitalization, innovation and the adoption of alternative marine fuels further strengthen the ecosystem and create new opportunities for maritime businesses. November 13, 2026 © Port Of Los Angeles/Port Of Long Beach The Port of Los Angeles and Port of Long Beach will commemorate the 20th anniversary of the landmark Clean Air Action Plan (CAAP) with a special stakeholder meeting and harbor tour of the entire San Pedro Bay port complex aboard El Escudo , Harbor Breeze’s new zero-emission excursion vessel, on Wednesday Dec. 2 from 9:30 a.m. to noon, weather permitting. First adopted in 2006 and last updated in 2017, the CAAP is a comprehensive strategy for accelerating progress toward a zero-emissions future, while protecting and strengthening the ports’ competitive position in the global economy. Since 2005, port-related air pollution emissions in San Pedro Bay have dropped 90% for diesel particulate matter, 71% for nitrogen oxides, and 98% for sulfur oxides. Targets for reducing greenhouse gases (GHG) from port-related sources were introduced as part of the 2017 CAAP. The document calls for the Ports to reduce GHG 40% below 1990 levels by 2030 and 80% below 1990 levels by 2050. Boat tour attendees will meet at Banning’s Landing Community Center, 100 E. If you will be unable to board the vessel at this location due to a physical ailment, indicate this via the registration form at least one week before the event to arrange alternate accommodations. articles.title: Singapore-Registered Bulk Carrier Strikes US Bridge, Disrupts Traffic
articles.summary: The Singapore-registered bulk carrier STRATEGIC ALLIANCE has struck the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge over the Delaware River between Pennsylvania and New Jersey, forcing a temporary closure before vehicle traffic was partially restored.The incident occurred shortly after 1 p.m.
articles.body: Singapore-Registered Bulk Carrier Strikes US Bridge, Disrupts Traffic Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 13, 2026 The Tacony-Palmyra Bridge spanning the Delaware River between Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and Palmyra, New Jersey, pictured in June 2010 (Credit: Jag9889 / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0) The Singapore-registered bulk carrier STRATEGIC ALLIANCE has struck the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge over the Delaware River between Pennsylvania and New Jersey, forcing a temporary closure before vehicle traffic was partially restored. The incident occurred shortly after 1 p.m. local time on November 12 during a bridge opening for marine traffic, according to the Burlington County Bridge Commission. Representative Ed Neilson reported that the bridge was initially unable to close following the collision, causing significant traffic congestion on the Philadelphia side. The bridge was closed to motorists and pedestrians while officials investigated potential structural damage. Subsequent inspections indicated that the bridge was safe and that the damage appeared minor, the commission said. By 8:40 p.m., two lanes had reopened to motor vehicles, one in each direction, although another lane remained closed for repairs to the pedestrian sidewalk. Pedestrian access to the bridge remained prohibited. Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) confirmed that STRATEGIC ALLIANCE was involved in the incident, reporting no injuries to civilians or crew members, no major damage to the vessel and no marine pollution. The bulk carrier is safely moored at the Kinder Morgan terminal in Pennsylvania, according to MPA. The Singaporean authority said it was in contact with the vessel's management company and relevant US authorities to establish the circumstances of the incident and would conduct an investigation. Repairs and inspections of the bridge are continuing.

articles.body: Interconnectors November 13, 2026 · 1 minute ago Orkney Islands’ first link to UK mainland nears offshore installation NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 1 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Nexans via LinkedIn Nexans has completed the factory acceptance test (FAT) of the 220 kV subsea cable that will connect the Orkney Islands to the UK mainland for the first time, in preparation for offshore installation that will start next year. According to the company, the completion of the FAT testing represents the culmination of more than a year of manufacturing activities at its facility in Halden, Norway. "With this important manufacturing milestone achieved, project activities continue to progress on several fronts. Nexans started the installation of the underground land cable for the electricity interconnector this September. The installation will be done in phases, beginning in the east and progressing west towards Warebeth, where the cable will connect with the project’s future subsea section. articles.title: Seaway7 Starts Cable Installation at Ørsted’s Hornsea 3 Wind Farm
articles.summary: Seaway7 has installed the first inter-array cable at Ørsted's 2.9 GW Hornsea 3 offshore wind farm in the UK North Sea, marking the start of a major cable installation campaign.The company will transport and install more than 536 kilometers of 66kV inter-array cables…
articles.body: Seaway7 Starts Cable Installation at Ørsted’s Hornsea 3 Wind Farm Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 13, 2026 (Credit: Seaway7) Seaway7 has installed the first inter-array cable at Ørsted's 2.9 GW Hornsea 3 offshore wind farm in the UK North Sea, marking the start of a major cable installation campaign. The company will transport and install more than 536 kilometers of 66kV inter-array cables, connecting the wind turbines to offshore converter stations, Seaway7 announced on November 12. The scope covers 197 inter-array cables at Hornsea 3, which Seaway7 expects to become the world's largest offshore wind farm when completed. The project is the third in Ørsted's Hornsea offshore wind zone for which Seaway7 has secured an inter-array cable installation contract. The company previously transported and installed 89 cables totaling approximately 170 kilometers at Hornsea 1, followed by 165 cables spanning around 382 kilometers at Hornsea 2. Once the latest campaign is completed, Seaway7 will have installed more than 1,000 kilometers of inter-array cables across the three developments. The Hornsea projects are located approximately 90 - 160 kilometers off the east coast of England, in water depths ranging from around 25 to 75 meters. Delivery of the current installation program is being led from Seaway7's Aberdeen office.
